listen_ipv4.description: IPv4 address and port for the tracker to listen on (e.g., '0.0.0.0:6969').

listen_ipv6.description: IPv6 address and port for the tracker to listen on (e.g., '[::]:6969'). Leave empty to disable IPv6.

bind_address.description: Specific interface(s) to bind to (e.g., 'eth0'). Leave empty to bind to all interfaces.

max_connections_per_ip.description: Maximum number of simultaneous connections allowed per IP address. Set to 0 for unlimited.

max_peers_per_torrent.description: Maximum number of peers returned per torrent in the response. Set to 0 for unlimited.

data_dir.description: Path to directory for persistent state (e.g., torrent counters). Disable if empty (in-memory only).

acl_file.description: Path to file containing allowed peer IDs or IPs (one per line). Disable if empty (no ACL).

announce_interval.description: Default announce interval (in seconds) to suggest to clients (e.g., 1800 = 30 minutes).

min_announce_interval.description: Minimum interval (seconds) clients must wait between announces. Prevents excessive requests.

scramble_peers.description: Enable scrambling of peer lists to reduce automated spam/bot trackers.

compact_list.description: Enable compact peer list format (6 bytes per peer) to reduce bandwidth usage.

partial_peers.description: Support for partial peers (used for magnet link support). Enable only if needed.

scrape_enabled.description: Enable the /scrape endpoint for statistics about torrent counts and completions.

ssl_enabled.description: Enable TLS/SSL for HTTPS support. Requires valid certificate and key paths.

ssl_cert.description: Path to SSL certificate file (PEM format). Required if SSL is enabled.

ssl_key.description: Path to SSL private key file (PEM format). Required if SSL is enabled.

log_file.description: Path to log file. Leave empty to log to stderr.

allowed_announce_urls.description: List of announce URLs (domains) that clients are allowed to use. Empty = allow any announce URL (open tracker).

announce_rate_limit.description: Maximum announces per IP per second (0 = no rate limiting). Helps prevent abuse.
